body:
Applicable host-contract version for this workspace's integration: **1** (HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION generation 1).

Determination (pinned artifact is decisive, and it is locally inspectable):
1. Engine artifact actually pinned: `node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/host.js` declares `export const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1;`, and `assertHostContract(v)` throws `HostContractMismatchError` unless `v === 1` (exact match, no tolerance layer). `@ordarium/core` is the single installed copy, at version 1.3.1. `@ordarium/host-kit` 1.3.1 (`dist/src/index.js`) is a curated re-export of exactly that constant/function from `@ordarium/core` — so the kit cannot supply a different generation.
2. Workspace-side pin: `src/effects/runtime.ts:128` calls the literal `assertHostContract(1)` at assembly (commented per PLMP-CONF-1 §1 as the fail-closed literal — a generation change fails assembly until consciously updated). `test/host_conformance.test.ts` (CONF-A01) pins `assertHostContract(1)` OK and `assertHostContract(2)` throwing.
3. Dependency pins resolve to that same engine: `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` both pin all four `@ordarium/*` tarballs at `ordarium-v1.3.1`.

Conflict handling (local precedence, no peer contact needed): the only source asserting "2" is `docs/engineering/notes/host-contract-note.md`, which is self-labeled "informational, not normative" and describes an *early* note — i.e. not co-applicable as a binding version statement. It is superseded by (a) the pinned engine artifact's own declaration, (b) the load-bearing fail-closed code literal and its test, and (c) the cross-repo charter `docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md` (r10, r19), which records explicitly that there is no HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION→2 plan. `docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md` (§0 "contract generation 1", §1.1 literal `1`, §2 no compatibility layer) and `docs/engineering/00-heritage.md` (R17) state the integration was built and tested against generation 1.

Precedence chain applied: self-declared non-normative early note < executable, machine-enforced handshake in the pinned dependency + the workspace's own pinning literal + the coordination charter. The residual difference is resolved by provenance/scope (a non-normative historical memo vs. the current executed contract), so no unresolved load-bearing conflict remains for the peer to arbitrate.
